entities.summary: Aleksandr Mikhailovich Sakharovsky was a Soviet general who was head of the First Chief Directorate of the KGB from 1955 to 1971. Sakharovsky oversaw the KGB foreign intelligence division during some of the key events of the Cold War, including the Hungarian uprising, the Cuban Missile Crisis and the height of the Vietnam War.
